description: The 9 February Baku family action is documented with a domestic political demand, but its crowd size is not reported. The US Embassy venue alone cannot identify the demand recipient; the VOA account supplies the domestic-state link through the family representative's prior approaches to Azerbaijani offices.
required_followup: Seek contemporaneous attendance evidence and confirm any additional direct demand recipient without treating the embassy venue as dispositive.

description: For 9 February, police took and tore signs/photos, but the source does not establish crowd dispersal, physical end, or the other state-response dimensions. The embassy's separate statement is not an Azerbaijani government response.
required_followup: Find event-specific reporting on the gathering's end and Azerbaijani police/government conduct; retain unknown state-response values until then.

description: The 1 February Lankaran report names four detained activists, while one participant account says three were together at detention. About 100 refers to student complaints, not protest turnout. Recovered Turan headers titled “Student activist detained in Lankaran” and “PCTA supported the initiative of students in Lankaran” add search-only leads, but no captured date, body or exact story link establishes their relation to the 1 February action. No source establishes total attendance or 50 people; the OC Media URL has an observed 403 in the January unit.
required_followup: Find an accessible contemporaneous attendance account or retain the event outside the candidate set; preserve the 3/4 detention distinction and do not substitute complaint volume. If either Turan lead is pursued, establish its date and story relationship from the body before treating it as event evidence or corroboration.

description: For the 4 February feminist action, VOA and OC Media place participants at Government House; the later COI report says parliament/SCFWCA. S004 links its interviewee to VOA, so those reports are not independent. Police took the banner/posters, but the available accounts do not establish protest-time state killings or a physical end.
required_followup: Resolve venue from original contemporary reporting and trace the COI footnote's OC Media/JAMnews citations; do not count search-only Caucasian Knot variants as independent evidence.

description: The COI report describes about ten female relatives at the US Embassy on 19 February and police stopping the action after ten minutes. A Toplum search preview appears to describe that dated event, but its body is inaccessible; Caucasian Knot search titles may concern one or both prisoner-family actions. Their exact story relationships and any relation to 9 February remain unresolved.
required_followup: Open or otherwise verify the original reports under a fresh access check; identify organizers, demands, attendance and whether the 9 and 19 February actions are distinct.

description: AzTV/Bia search-result titles describe an individual woman’s complaint/action and an attempted self-immolation; bodies were not accessible. S009 carries a 2021-02-09 publication date copied from the January unit’s alternate AzTV URL, while S010 has no captured publication date; neither date establishes incident onset. The January unit’s 8 February continuation lead is also unverified; a January 8 progress-note entry was a transcription error, not event evidence.
required_followup: If accessible reporting is found, verify incident date, public assembly, audience of the demand and attendance before reconsidering the lead.

description: The later Netherlands COI report provides the 6 and about-10 counts and cites media footnotes; the originals behind its 19 February citation were not read. Scholars at Risk's Lankaran summary draws on ACLED and local reports, so it is derivative rather than independent turnout confirmation. OC Media S004 itself says its interviewee had also spoken to VOA.

description: This is an English/Azerbaijani/Russian open-web first pass with generic, weekly, regional, sectoral and episode-detail searches. Forty-seven responses are captured: forty-six with result headers and one explicit empty response (Q040), totaling 906 aligned headers. Five early responses were recovered as Q042-Q046; full capture recovery restored 27 of the 46 saved rows from their original worker search events and appended one previously uncaptured response as AZERBAIJAN-RECOVER-001, while preserving the other 19 rows. Q040 matched the captured empty response and was not duplicated. Search providers expose no result totals. Cache misses and DNS errors occurred before HTTP, and no LexisNexis-scale archive was available, so results are not exhaustive.
required_followup: Continue bounded open-web searches and inspect unverified sources under fresh receipts, including the restored Milli.az and police-relocation leads and Turan/OC Media/JAMnews search-only titles. Do not infer an event, episode relationship, month ownership or absence from search silence.
